/-!
# Conjecture 9.7

by R. I. Grigorchuk

(A. M. Stëpin). Does there exist an infinite finitely generated amenable group of
bounded exponent?

A group has bounded exponent if there is a positive integer $n$ with $g^n = 1$ for
every element $g$. Without the amenability hypothesis the answer is known to be
positive: the free Burnside groups $B(m, n)$ of Novikov–Adian and Ol'shanskii are
infinite, finitely generated and of bounded exponent, but they are not amenable.
Mathlib has no notion of an amenable group, so amenability is defined here for
discrete groups via a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on all
subsets of the group (von Neumann's definition).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

def IsAmenable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ m : Set G → ℝ≥0∞, m Set.univ = 1 ∧
    (∀ s t : Set G, Disjoint s t → m (s ∪ t) = m s + m t) ∧
    ∀ (g : G) (s : Set G), m (g • s) = m s
blocks.docstring:
A (discrete) group $G$ is *amenable* if there is a left-invariant finitely additive
probability measure defined on all subsets of $G$: a function
$m \colon \mathcal{P}(G) \to [0, \infty]$ with $m(G) = 1$, $m(S \cup T) = m(S) + m(T)$
for disjoint $S, T \subseteq G$, and $m(gS) = m(S)$ for all $g \in G$ and $S \subseteq G$.
Here `g • s` is the left translate $gS = \{g x \mid x \in S\}$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `IsFoelner` / `maxFoelner` (MeasureTheory/Group/FoelnerFilter.lean): these define Følner sequences/filters for a group acting on a measure space but no standalone amenability predicate; one could say `NeBot (maxFoelner G (Measure.count))`, but that is a sufficient condition phrased via a measure-space action rather than the standard invariant-mean definition, and it would be less transparent for a discrete group.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.7».IsAmenable
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no amenability predicate (FoelnerFilter.lean explicitly says a definition has not yet been given); the repo has none either. Defined as ∃ m : Set G → ℝ≥0∞, m univ = 1 ∧ (∀ s t, Disjoint s t → m (s ∪ t) = m s + m t) ∧ ∀ g s, m (g • s) = m s, i.e. a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on P(G) — the standard definition of amenability for discrete groups, and the exact shape of the conclusion of Mathlib's `IsFoelner.amenable`/`amenable_of_maxFoelner_neBot`. A small API theorem `IsAmenable.of_finite` (finite groups are amenable via normalised counting measure) is included as a sanity test.

blocks.name: IsAmenable
blocks.text:
/--
A (discrete) group $G$ is *amenable* if there is a left-invariant finitely additive
probability measure defined on all subsets of $G$: a function
$m \colon \mathcal{P}(G) \to [0, \infty]$ with $m(G) = 1$, $m(S \cup T) = m(S) + m(T)$
for disjoint $S, T \subseteq G$, and $m(gS) = m(S)$ for all $g \in G$ and $S \subseteq G$.
Here `g • s` is the left translate $gS = \{g x \mid x \in S\}$.
-/
def IsAmenable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ m : Set G → ℝ≥0∞, m Set.univ = 1 ∧
    (∀ s t : Set G, Disjoint s t → m (s ∪ t) = m s + m t) ∧
    ∀ (g : G) (s : Set G), m (g • s) = m s

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 20 43]
theorem IsAmenable.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsAmenable G := by
  have hG : (Nat.card G : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast Nat.card_pos.ne'
  refine ⟨fun s => (s.ncard : ℝ≥0∞) / Nat.card G, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [Set.ncard_univ, ENNReal.div_self hG (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top _)]
  · intro s t hst
    simp [Set.ncard_union_eq hst, ENNReal.add_div]
  · intro g s
    simp [Set.ncard_smul_set]
blocks.docstring:
Every finite group is amenable: normalised counting measure is a left-invariant
finitely additive probability measure.

claims.decomposer_note: Single unlettered yes/no existence question (no \zva star, no lettered parts): the Prop is ∃ G, Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ G amenable ∧ Monoid.ExponentExists G; 'bounded exponent' means some positive n with g^n = 1 for all g (equivalently a finitely generated infinite amenable torsion group of bounded exponent, i.e. an amenable counterexample to the Burnside problem), and since Mathlib has no standalone `Amenable` predicate (only Følner-filter results in MeasureTheory/Group/FoelnerFilter.lean) amenability must be defined explicitly, e.g. via a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure / mean on all subsets of the discrete group G, or via Følner sequences.; note the answer for 'finitely generated' without amenability is yes (Novikov–Adian/Olshanskii free Burnside groups, which are non-amenable), so the amenability hypothesis is essential and must not be dropped.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the identical, faithful core theorem `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsAmenable G ∧ Monoid.ExponentExists G`. Verified: `Monoid.ExponentExists G` is `∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∀ g, g ^ n = 1` (bounded exponent, positivity excludes n = 0); `Group.FG` is finite generation; `answer(True)` = positive answer; conjunction inside the existential (no `∃ x, P x → Q` pitfall). Amenability has no Mathlib predicate (only Følner-filter results), so it is defined bespoke via von Neumann's left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on all subsets; `g • s` is by `rfl` the left translate `(g * ·) '' s`; the `ℝ≥0∞` codomain is forced ≤ 1 by `m univ = 1` and finite additivity, so it is equivalent to c08's real-valued variant and matches Mathlib's `IsFoelner.amenable` conclusion. c05 chosen over the equivalent c03/c04 (Mathlib-style dot-name `IsAmenable.of_finite`, `category API`), over c01/c02/c06/c07 (which lack the API test CONTRIBUTING.md requests for bespoke definitions), and over c08 (ℝ-valued mean with extra nonnegativity clause; equivalent but less aligned with Mathlib). Minor docstring edits only; compiles with only the `sorry` warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.7

by R. I. Grigorchuk

(A. M. Stëpin). Does there exist an infinite finitely generated amenable group of
bounded exponent?

A group has bounded exponent if there is a positive integer $n$ with $g^n = 1$ for
every element $g$. Without the amenability hypothesis the answer is known to be
positive: the free Burnside groups $B(m, n)$ of Novikov–Adian and Ol'shanskii are
infinite, finitely generated and of bounded exponent, but they are not amenable.
Mathlib has no notion of an amenable group, so amenability is defined here for
discrete groups via a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on all
subsets of the group (von Neumann's definition).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped ENNReal Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«9.7»

/--
A (discrete) group $G$ is *amenable* if there is a left-invariant finitely additive
probability measure defined on all subsets of $G$: a function
$m \colon \mathcal{P}(G) \to [0, \infty]$ with $m(G) = 1$, $m(S \cup T) = m(S) + m(T)$
for disjoint $S, T \subseteq G$, and $m(gS) = m(S)$ for all $g \in G$ and $S \subseteq G$.
Here `g • s` is the left translate $gS = \{g x \mid x \in S\}$.
-/
def IsAmenable (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ m : Set G → ℝ≥0∞, m Set.univ = 1 ∧
    (∀ s t : Set G, Disjoint s t → m (s ∪ t) = m s + m t) ∧
    ∀ (g : G) (s : Set G), m (g • s) = m s

/-- Every finite group is amenable: normalised counting measure is a left-invariant
finitely additive probability measure. -/
@[category API, AMS 20 43]
theorem IsAmenable.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsAmenable G := by
  have hG : (Nat.card G : ℝ≥0∞) ≠ 0 := by
    exact_mod_cast Nat.card_pos.ne'
  refine ⟨fun s => (s.ncard : ℝ≥0∞) / Nat.card G, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [Set.ncard_univ, ENNReal.div_self hG (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top _)]
  · intro s t hst
    simp [Set.ncard_union_eq hst, ENNReal.add_div]
  · intro g s
    simp [Set.ncard_smul_set]

/--
(A. M. Stëpin). Does there exist an infinite finitely generated amenable group of
bounded exponent?

Here "bounded exponent" means that there is a positive integer $n$ with $g^n = 1$ for
all $g \in G$ (`Monoid.ExponentExists G`), and "amenable" is `IsAmenable G`, the
existence of a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on all subsets
of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20 43]
theorem kourovka.«9.7» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsAmenable G ∧ Monoid.ExponentExists G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.7»

items: Amenability is modelled via a left-invariant finitely additive probability measure on all subsets of G (values in ℝ≥0∞ with m univ = 1, matching Mathlib's Følner file). For discrete groups this is equivalent to the invariant-mean-on-ℓ^∞ and Følner-sequence definitions; left vs right invariance is immaterial for groups.
`g • s` is the pointwise left translate {g * x | x ∈ s} (verified: x ∈ g • s ↔ ∃ y ∈ s, g * y = x), so invariance is left-invariance.
Bounded exponent is `Monoid.ExponentExists G` (∃ n, 0 < n ∧ ∀ g, g ^ n = 1); the positivity requirement excludes the degenerate n = 0.

The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files (1_74, 19_25); this loses nothing since any group is equivalent to one in Type 0 via cardinality only if small — but every counterexample of interest is countable, and the repo consistently uses `Type`.
AMS tags 20 (group theory) and 43 (abstract harmonic analysis, where amenability 43A07 lives).

reviewer_notes: Single-slot yes/no existence question; no ambiguity in the source. The essential amenability hypothesis is retained (dropping it would make the answer trivially yes via free Burnside groups). The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the Kourovka idiom (1_74, 19_25); this loses no generality since finitely generated groups are countable. The bespoke `IsAmenable` is kept in the problem file because the pipeline writes a single file; in a real PR it could move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. No candidate omitted the slot; all reports were consistent with their Lean text.
